QUOTE: The code is split by mask. The high-level part is `ret & 0xFF80` (the module, e.g. CIPHER, DHM, SSL). The low-level part is `ret & ~0xFF80` (the specific error within it). ... If both parts exist, they are joined as `"<high> : <low>"` in `buf`.
VERDICT: HIT
WHY: The answer states that a code splits into high-level (module) and low-level parts and that strerror joins both when both are present.
